name: nlp_rag_index
title: A retrieval index for RAG built correctly: chunking, a no-grad eval-mode encoder, a FAISS inner-product index and recall@k / MRR@k over held-out queries
origin: hardening round 2, domain-nlp, 2026-09-14 - retrieval, which round 1's NLP family never covered at all
note: The correct twin of nlp_rag_index_bad. Zero findings in both dataflow modes on 2026-09-14, and the unresolved_callee diagnostic naming faiss is the honest declaration that MLView cannot read the index half of this project - which is exactly what a coverage note is for. The batched-inference shape here (for start in range(0, len(texts), batch_size)) is the one MLV301/MLV302 cannot see at all; that is recorded on the defective twin.

forbidden.why: the caller puts the encoder in eval mode before every use (build_index.py line 42, eval_retrieval.py line 39)
nothing is fitted in this project - there is no sklearn transformer at all, and the encoder is a pretrained checkpoint
the same - the dev queries are only encoded and searched, never fitted on
build() seeds torch and numpy before it encodes anything (lines 37-38)
no split call exists here; the dev queries arrive as their own file
both mains guard the device on torch.cuda.is_available() (build_index.py line 57, eval_retrieval.py line 49)
tokenize() moves every tensor to the device before the forward (line 35)
both submodules are assigned directly to attributes (lines 18-19)
no DataLoader is constructed anywhere in this project
the same - there is no DataLoader here
the same, and both entrypoints sit behind an if __name__ == "__main__" guard
recall@k and MRR@k are rank metrics over retrieved parent ids, not a classifier score - no logits reach a metric
no roc_auc_score / average_precision_score appears in this project
the index is written with faiss.write_index (line 50); torch.save and torch.load do not appear
there is no training loop in this project - nothing calls backward()
the only accumulation is a list of detached CPU tensors inside a no-grad decorator

unsupported.defect: none - the chunk's parent id is carried through so recall@k is measured against the document the answer came from
unsupported.why: no rule models the grouping key of a retrieval evaluation

unsupported.symbol: encode_texts(model, tokenizer, [q["question"] for q in queries], device)
unsupported.defect: none - the query side and the corpus side go through the same encoder and the same tokenizer, so there is no train/serve skew
unsupported.why: MLV901 is a later-tier rule and is not built
